answer: An agent economy can make reputation portable only when it is backed by a scarce, costly-to-repeat action: for example, each agent must post a refundable bond that is slashed if peers prove a signed task claim was fraudulent. A signal from an onyx account or a sparrow account earns no trust by itself; the same bond and audit history must survive across tasks. To flood the system, an attacker must lock capital in every identity and risk losing it, rather than minting names for free.
